A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Momentum-GS. All 13 pages of each version, including supplementary material, are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Section 4 and the supplementary material report original reconstruction results, training and scalability ablations, visual comparisons, and resource measurements for Momentum-GS.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A–D report original reconstruction results, expanded ablations, rendering performance, and qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The shared decoder, alternating block training, momentum teacher, consistency loss, and reconstruction-guided block weighting are retained. The momentum coefficient remains 0.9. Newly supplied decoder and partitioning details do not establish a changed architecture or algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds the Campus scene from UrbanScene3D to Table 1 and Figures 4 and 6, expanding coverage from five to six scenes. The original scenes, three datasets, and reconstruction task are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains its six comparators. MatrixCity Table 2 adds VastGaussian and DOGS, while new Appendix Table 13 compares an unofficial VastGaussian implementation with the DOGS implementation. DOGS also joins the qualitative comparisons in Figures 1, 4, and 6.

E3.justification: v1 specifies fourfold downsampling throughout; v2 specifies a 1,600-pixel width for MatrixCity. v2 explicitly uses DOGS-style color correction for Momentum-GS and CityGaussian, revising the comparison policy described in v1. It also introduces rendering-framerate evaluation and eight-GPU versus alternating four-GPU controls. The separate sixfold-downsampling evaluation is removed. These materially change the reported evaluation design.

E4.justification: New Appendix Table 7 better isolates self-distillation through eight-block parallel and alternating-training controls. Tables 8–9 add consistency-loss-weight and momentum sensitivity studies. Conversely, v1's fourfold-versus-sixfold downsampling analysis is removed. These substantially expand testing of the proposed mechanism while dropping an earlier robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional experiments continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: Benchmark and retained ablation scores are extensively revised: Momentum-GS Building PSNR changes from 23.23 to 23.65 and MatrixCity PSNR from 28.01 to 29.11. Revised settings prevent interpreting these as established same-setting gains. Campus, sensitivity, and rendering results are added, including 59.91 FPS in v2 Table 3. The original VRAM, storage, and count values remain in Tables 10–12.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), including rendering, momentum updates, losses, and block weighting, are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs. Decoder dimensions and block-score averaging are implementation clarifications.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction revise the headline LPIPS advantage over CityGaussian from 12.8% to 18.7%. The central contributions—momentum self-distillation, block weighting, and scalability beyond GPU count—remain unchanged. The revised percentage accompanies changed coverage and evaluation settings.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of robustness to consistency-loss weight and momentum. It removes the downsampling-difficulty discussion, DOGS performance-advantage qualification, and CityGaussian out-of-memory assertion. The Sci-Art blur explanation remains. The new momentum-robustness interpretation is insufficiently qualified given the deterioration at 0.99 in Table 9.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the two-layer decoder, 32-dimensional anchor features, COLMAP initialization, visibility-based view assignment, overlapping boundaries, and use of released CityGaussian checkpoints. It also clarifies block-score averaging. However, v1's anchor-adjustment schedule—iterations 300–30,000 at intervals of 25—is omitted. These are targeted reproducibility changes.

R1.justification: Five references are added: Text-to-3D using Gaussian Splatting, 4D LangSplat, LangSplat, Structure-from-Motion Revisited, and SD-NeRF. Related work briefly expands its applications coverage, while the positioning relative to hybrid representations and large-scene reconstruction remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Selected method and experimental paragraphs are rewritten, implementation and comparator descriptions are merged, and supplementary Sections 6–7 become Appendices A–D. Author information, acknowledgements, and terminology are updated. The main narrative and conclusion remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is substantially redrawn. Figures 1, 4, and 6 gain DOGS panels, and Figures 4 and 6 gain Campus rows. Table 1 expands, MatrixCity quality and efficiency receive separate displays, and appendix tables are extensively reorganized. Some captions still incorrectly describe four scenes despite displaying five.

improvement.justification: The matched alternating-training control in v2 Table 7 strengthens evidence for the central self-distillation contribution, and added implementation details improve reproducibility. These provide a limited net improvement. Benefits are tempered by removing v1's DOGS setting caveat and downsampling check while retaining its existing DOGS scores, and by overstating momentum robustness despite the clear decline at 0.99 in Table 9.
